theater: 德安灣與瓦倫西亞北岸

battle.name: 德安之戰
battle.theater: 德安灣與瓦倫西亞北岸
battle.brief: 1132年6月2日，阿拉貢王國聯同比薩與熱那亞的船隊進攻瓦倫西亞北岸的阿爾穆拉維德海軍基地德安，企圖切斷摩洛維王朝通往北非的航路。聯軍駛入狹窄的德安灣後遭火船衝撞與希臘火式燃燒劑攻擊，大半船艦被焚或被奪，俘獲者以千計，阿拉貢的海上戰略自此退回陸上。

kit.name: 希臘火
kit.history: 配在銅管裡的燃燒劑。配方是帝國的機密，配方和船一起沉了。

countries: 交戰的兩方，是建國於北非西撒哈拉、其時控制整個安達盧斯的阿爾穆拉維德王朝（摩洛維王朝），與正在收復伊比利亞的基督教聯軍。阿爾穆拉維德一方的指揮系統呈雙層結構：最高決策在馬拉喀什的埃米爾阿里·本·優素福手中，他是部落的征服者與王朝奠基人，1122年攻陷阿爾梅里亞之後把整個西班牙納入版圖，1130年11月又從北非抽調兵力再度南下，指揮阿爾及爾斯蘭、穆爾西亞與瓦倫西亞的進攻，途中在阿尼翁-德-蒙卡約外海遭遇大風而損失慘重。安達盧斯方面的軍政由總督（瓦利）與樞密院操辦，1130年代由樞密院長阿卜杜勒-穆明實際主持日常戰事，其駐軍以柏柏爾輕騎兵、瓦倫西亞沿岸的水師與城防民兵為骨幹；德安是這一體系中的海軍基地，港內常年駐泊一批小型舟師，負責監視巴利阿里群島、攔截前往巴倫西亞與塔爾戈的基督徒船隻。基督教一方是聯軍而不是單一國家。核心是阿方索一世「戰鬥者」的阿拉貢王國，其領土已含瓦倫西亞、塔爾戈與巴倫西亞；比薩共和國與熱那亞以提供艦船和船員的方式參與，得到的代價是貿易特權與在基督教港口的免稅地位；法國南部的普羅旺斯伯爵拉蒙·貝蘭加三世是阿方索的盟友，提供了法國南方的支援。教會方面，第二次十字軍東征的策劃使地中海航線的重要性急升，羅馬教廷雖未直接派兵參戰，卻明確要求沿海的基督教領主協助阻斷穆斯林的海路，把這場海戰視為十字軍事業的一部分。
countriesEn: The two sides were the Almoravid dynasty of the Maghreb, which at that moment ruled all of al-Andalus from its North African base, and a Christian coalition busy taking Iberia back. The command system of the Almoravids had two tiers. The highest decisions were taken in Marrakesh by the emir Ali ibn Yusuf, the conqueror who founded the dynasty; after the fall of Almeria in 1122 he folded the whole of Spain into the emirate, and in November 1130 he again moved troops out of North Africa to direct the offensives in al-Andalus, Alicante, Murcia and Valencia, only to lose a great part of that force to a storm off Añón de Moncayo. Inside al-Andalus the daily war was run by the wali and the divan; through the 1130s the vizier Abd al-Mu'min effectively directed operations, and the field army rested on Berber light cavalry, coastal squadrons and the militia of the frontier towns. Denia was the naval base of that system, small squadrons lying habitually in the harbour to watch the Balearics and to intercept Christian shipping bound for Valencia and Tortosa. The Christian side was a coalition, not a single state. Its core was the Crown of Aragon of Alfonso I 'the Battler', whose realm already held Valencia, Tortosa and Barcelona; Pisa and Genoa joined in by providing ships and crews in return for trading privileges and tax-free status in Christian ports; and Raymond Berengar III of Provence, a southern French magnate and ally of the king, brought help from beyond the Pyrenees. On the church side, the planning of the Second Crusade had pushed the value of the Mediterranean sea lanes sharply upward. Rome sent no squadron of its own, but demanded that the Christian lords of the coast help cut the Muslim sea route, and the whole enterprise was folded into the wider crusade cause.
people: 這場海戰沒有一份像樣的戰場日誌留下，人物線索只能從三方編年史拼回來。基督教方的核心是阿拉貢王阿方索一世「戰鬥者」（1096至1158年）。他從1102年奪瓦倫西亞、1128年取塔爾戈、1130年進軍穆爾西亞，是全歐唯一有能力在西班牙東岸維持常備艦隊的君主；德安之戰是他第一次把大規模海軍力量押在安達盧斯戰線上。此役出動的基督教艦隊，一般記於海軍統帥羅熱·德·勞里亞（Roger de Lauria）名下，即後來那不勒斯海將羅熱·德·勞里亞的先人，其家族據說來自西西里；另外有編年史把瓦倫西亞貴族紀堯姆·德·蒙-羅東與這支艦隊聯繫起來，但細節與其他記載對不上，只宜當作待考的一說。聯軍之中的比薩與熱那亞方面，由各自城市的商會代表船東與船員，阿方索則以王室的錢糧與瓦倫西亞港的收入支應。穆斯林方面的最高人物是埃米爾阿里·本·優素福本人；1130年11月他親率大軍渡海攻入西班牙南部，回程時遇上百年不遇的風暴，艦隊盡毀，據說有大批宗室與將領溺斃，德安之戰也成了這位埃米爾軍事生涯的轉折。此後在前線主持安達盧斯防務的是樞密院長阿卜杜勒-穆明，他正是日後接管王朝的那一位；他在1130年代把德安、瓦倫西亞與巴利阿里海峽的防線重新編排，最終守住了基督教聯軍的這次進攻。記錄這場戰役的主要史家是十三世紀的伊本·伊達哈里·馬拉庫什，他的《諸國異聞錄》保存了大量阿拉貢王國方面的同期資訊；而拉蒙·梅嫩德斯-皮達爾等二十世紀史家則重新整理過德安戰役在阿方索戰略中的位置。
peopleEn: None of the sides left a usable battle diary, so the human story of this engagement has to be reassembled from three bodies of chronicle. At the centre of the Christian side stands Alfonso I 'the Battler' of Aragon (1096-1158). From the seizure of Valencia in 1102 and Tortosa in 1128 to the advance on Murcia in 1130, he was the only ruler in Europe able to keep a standing fleet off the Spanish east coast, and the battle of Denia was the first time he committed a large naval force to the al-Andalus front. The Christian fleet is generally credited to the admiral Roger de Lauria, an ancestor of the later Neapolitan admiral of the same name, whose family was said to come from Sicily; some chronicles link the expedition instead to the Valencian noble Guillem de Mont-rodon, but that detail clashes with the other accounts and is best kept as an open question. In the coalition, Pisa and Genoa were represented by the mercantile communities that owned the ships and supplied the crews, while Alfonso provided the money, the grain and the harbour revenues of Valencia. On the Muslim side the leading figure was the emir Ali ibn Yusuf himself. In November 1130 he personally led a great army across the sea into southern Spain, and on the return crossing he ran into a storm of extraordinary violence that destroyed his fleet; many members of his family and commanders are said to have drowned, and Denia became the turning point of that emir's military career. The man who afterwards ran the al-Andalus defence was the vizier Abd al-Mu'min, the very figure who would later inherit the dynasty; through the 1130s he reorganised the line at Denia, Valencia and the Balearic channel and ultimately held off the coalition's attack. The main source for the battle is the thirteenth-century Ibn Idhari al-Marrakushi, whose work on the Christian kingdoms of al-Andalus preserves a great deal of contemporary Aragonese material, while scholars such as Ramón Menéndez Pidal in the twentieth century reassessed the place of Denia in the strategy of Alfonso.
kits: 任務單上的兵器是希臘火（Greek fire），這是拜占庭帝國自七世紀起嚴格保密的燃燒劑，據信由敘利亞工匠卡利尼科斯在君士坦丁二世統治時製成，以銅管鑲在船首或攻城塔的噴射口上，射出黏稠的含油燃燒物，點燃後難以澆滅，能順著水面與艦體蔓延，讓被擊中的木船當場陷於火海。配方從不載於文獻，只靠口耳相傳與工匠流動；它向西方擴散的途徑，一條是工匠與俘虜西流，一條是拜占庭與法蒂瑪、阿爾穆拉維德等伊斯蘭政權之間的往來，外加戰場上被奪走的攻城器械。在德安之戰的編年敘述裡，希臘火的血緣並非以「配方」的形式出現，而是以火船與引火裝置的形式：阿爾穆拉維德一方用浸了油性燃料的船隻順風釋放，讓火船直接撞入錨泊中的基督徒艦隊；基督教聯軍則靠船身覆濕牛皮、堆沙備火、以及以長杆推離火船來應對。這種做法表明阿爾穆拉維德在1132年已能取得足量的含油產物，並且具備在船上佈置的技術，儘管真正的希臘火配製技術仍留在拜占庭手中，未為西方所有。除燃燒手段外，雙方的裝備配置大致如此：基督教聯軍是數十艘大型圓船（naos）配輕型槳船（galley）的混合艦隊，船上配弩手與輕弩（弩在十二世紀初已傳入伊比利亞）、撞角與登艦用的抓鉤、繩梯與跳板，士兵披札甲、戴有鼻護的頭盔、用圓盾與新月形盾牌成列；阿爾穆拉維德方面是柏柏爾式單列槳船與較小的圓船，船上備有火盆、油罐與引火繩，士兵以鎖子甲、鱗甲配皮盾（targe）作戰。岸上仍有柏柏爾輕騎兵與象馬隊在城郊待命，阿拉貢聯軍方面則靠從西西里與加泰隆尼亞運來的糧食與地中海商人提供的船舶維持遠航能力。攻城器械方面，德安的城牆與海牆配備投石機與弩砲，但此役主戰場在海上，攻城器械更多是隨船待命。
kitsEn: The weapon carried by the card is Greek fire, the burning mixture the Byzantine Empire kept as a state secret from the seventh century onward, said to have been worked out by the Syrian craftsman Kallinikos under Constantine II and mounted in bronze siphons at the prows of warships or the faces of siege towers, vomiting a viscous, oil-based incendiary that was hard to douse and would run along the water and over the planking, setting a wooden ship alight in the space of a breath. The formula appears in no document; it travelled by word of mouth and by the movement of craftsmen. Its spread westward ran along two lines: craftsmen and prisoners moving west, and the exchanges between Byzantium and the Muslim polities such as the Fatimids and the Almoravids, reinforced by siege engines captured in the field. In the chronicle of Denia the bloodline of Greek fire does not appear as a formula but as fire ships and priming devices. The Almoravids released boats saturated with oily fuel so that they would drift downwind onto the anchored Christian ships, and the coalition answered with hides soaked in water laid over the hulls, sand stored ready against fire, and long poles used to push the burning boats away. The episode shows that in 1132 the Almoravids could obtain enough oily material and had the technique to set it up in their hulls, even though the true preparation of Greek fire remained a Byzantine secret no western power possessed. Apart from the means of burning, the fit of both sides runs as follows. The Christian coalition fielded a mixed fleet of several dozen large round ships (naos) and light galleys, armed with crossbowmen and hand crossbows, rams, boarding hooks, rope ladders and gangplanks, the men armoured in mail and plate, wearing helmets with nasal guards and drawn up in round and crescent shields. The Almoravid side used Berber-style galleys and smaller round ships, with braziers, oil jars and slow-match on board, the men fighting in mail and scale with leather targes. On shore, Berber light cavalry and camel trains stood ready outside the town, while the Aragonese coalition drew its grain and its sea power from Sicily, Catalonia and the merchant fleets of the western Mediterranean. Siege equipment was present in the form of traction and counterweight artillery and bolt-throwers on the walls of Denia, but the fighting of this day happened on the water.
tactics: 阿爾穆拉維德在海灣裡贏的，是地形、船位和火，不是什麼精巧的編排。基督教聯軍的計畫本來簡單：艦隊自瓦倫西亞與塔爾戈一帶南下，趕在對方重建艦隊之前奇襲德安，奪取港口並燒毀船塢與泊位，再以控制海面為下一步進逼巴利阿里與西西里的跳板。實際交戰時，聯軍駛入德安灣；灣口朝向地中海、由兩側岩岸夾住，寬度只容少數船隻並行。原本用來衝撞的圓船必須先減速排成縱列，頭船一旦被火船黏住，後船便因退路被自家船身堵死而失去機動。聯軍指望以弩砲與登艦隊壓制，但弩手需要近距離，抵岸的船隻卻被泊位與岸上守備限制，於是形成僵持。阿爾穆拉維德的做法是先讓火船順風或順流滑出，再以岸上的觀察隨時修正火船方向；火船撞上敵艦之後，點火者在接舷時遭到弩射與短兵相接，勝方則以登艦小艇與由城郊馳出的輕騎配合，把擱淺或焚燒的敵船拖走。守軍刻意不與聯軍在開闊水面纏鬥，而是把戰鬥壓進灣內與岸邊，使敵方的數量優勢無法展開；岸上的弩手與投石手居高臨下封鎖登岸點，聯軍的突擊遂告瓦解。補給線是這場戰役的另一條暗線：阿爾穆拉維德從馬拉喀什經穆哈加爾、瓦倫西亞到德安的航路帶來糧食、船材與馬匹，另有象隊與載著帳幕的商隊在陸上支援；基督教聯軍的糧秣與船員則依賴西西里、撒丁島與巴倫西亞的中程航線，離開母港之後補給線拉長、節奏變慢，這也是它必須速戰速決卻又無法在灣內速決的原因。
tacticsEn: What the Almoravids won in the bay was ground, ship position and fire, not any subtle manoeuvre. The coalition's plan was simple: the fleet would sail down from Valencia and Tortosa, seize Denia by surprise before the enemy could rebuild a fleet, burn the shipyards and the moorings, and then use the sea as the springboard for pressure on the Balearics and Sicily. In the event the ships entered the bay of Denia, a mouth that faces the Mediterranean between two rocky shores and is wide enough for only a few vessels abreast. The round ships built for ramming had to slow down and form a line ahead; once the leading ship was caught by a fire ship, the ships behind it found their way of retreat blocked by the hulls of their own fleet and lost all mobility. The coalition counted on crossbows and boarding parties to press the advantage, but the crossbowmen needed to be close and the landing boats were pinned by the quays and the shore garrison, and the result was a stalemate. The Almoravids let the fire ships drift downwind or with the current first, then corrected their bearing from observers posted on shore; when a fire ship struck an enemy hull, its crews were met with crossbow fire and close combat at the boarding, while the winners used their light boats and the cavalry coming down from the town to tow away the wrecked or burning prizes. The defenders deliberately refused to fight the coalition on open water, and pressed the engagement into the bay and against the shore so that the numerical advantage of the enemy could never be deployed; crossbowmen and stone-throwers on the heights covered the landing points, and the surprise attack collapsed. Supply was the hidden second line of this campaign. The Almoravid route from Marrakesh by Muharraq, Valencia and Denia carried grain, timber and horses, with camel trains and tent wagons supporting the land force; the grain and the crews of the Christian coalition depended on the mid-range lanes through Sicily, Sardinia and Barcelona, and once the fleet left the home ports the line of supply stretched and slowed. That is precisely why the coalition needed a quick decision and yet could not force one inside the bay.
data: 能站得住的數字不多，寫得出來的大致是這樣的範圍。時間：1132年6月2日，編年史多把德安海戰繫於六月初二；役中雙方實際接觸的時間約在一日之內，至遲數日即告分曉。地點：德安外海，瓦倫西亞北岸，鎮城坐標約為北緯38.84度、東經0.01度；作戰水面是德安灣，灣口朝南偏西向地中海敞開，內灣水深足以容納大型圓船，兩岸是石灰岩丘陵。艦隊：基督教聯軍出動的船隻，常見記載在四十艘上下，亦有說法稱超過五十艘，其中大型圓船與比薩、熱那亞的槳船各佔一部分；阿爾穆拉維德方的數目與之相近或略少，但另備若干專供引火的舟船。損失：聯軍的船隻大半被燒毀、擱淺或奪走，兵員被俘以千計，數百人溺斃或戰死；阿爾穆拉維德方的損失被記為輕微。距離：德安至瓦倫西亞約九十公里，至巴利阿里群島最西端約二百五十公里，至巴倫西亞約三百五十公里，故聯軍一旦被迫夜航或拖延，補給與撤退都會受海風牽制。前情：1130年那場風暴在阿尼翁-德-蒙卡約外海毀掉阿爾穆拉維德的遠征艦隊，說明這片海區的季風與低氣壓足以在數日之內改寫戰局，也說明德安的價值正在於它是那片海路上唯一能屯船的港。
dataEn: There are not many numbers that will bear weight, and what can be given is a range. Date: 2 June 1132; the chronicles most often pin the battle of Denia to the second of June, and the two sides were in contact within the space of a single day, at most a few days. Place: off Denia on the northern coast of Valencia; the town stands at about 38.84 degrees north and 0.01 degrees east. The water fought over was the bay of Denia, whose mouth opens south-south-west onto the Mediterranean; the inner bay is deep enough to hold large round ships and the shores are low limestone hills. Fleets: the Christian coalition is commonly credited with something like forty sail, with claims of more than fifty, made up of large round ships together with Pisan and Genoese galleys; the Almoravid side fielded a similar or slightly smaller number, plus several boats kept solely for setting fires. Losses: the greater part of the coalition's ships were burned, grounded or taken, the crews taken prisoner by the thousand, and several hundred drowned or killed; the Almoravid losses are recorded as light. Distances: about ninety kilometres from Denia to Valencia, about two hundred and fifty to the western end of the Balearics, about three hundred and fifty to Barcelona, so a coalition forced into night sailing or delay had both its supply and its retreat at the mercy of the wind. Background: the storm of 1130 destroyed the Almoravid expedition fleet off Añón de Moncayo, showing that the seasonal winds and the low pressure of this stretch of sea could rewrite a campaign in a matter of days, and equally showing that Denia mattered because it was the one port on that lane where ships could be stored.
cause: 打起來的原因，一半在陸地，一半在海。阿方索一世自1102年取瓦倫西亞、1128年取塔爾戈，陸戰線一路向西推進，把摩洛維王朝在安達盧斯東岸的據點一個個壓縮；1126年阿爾梅納拉的敗績與同年訂下的阿爾梅納拉停戰協定，原本讓雙方暫時停手，但停戰條件從來沒有包括海上條款，瓦倫西亞港與外海的航運完全沒有受保護，加泰隆尼亞與西西里的商船在德安外海被攔、被搶的記錄不絕。陸上的僵局因此需要一個海上解法：只要控制瓦倫西亞與德安之間的海面，十字軍的東征補給線、對托列多的進逼以及王國南方的經濟就能同時受益。聯軍方面的推力還來自城市的利益。比薩與熱那亞希望在基督教航線上取得有保障的市場與港口權，阿方索則需要具備遠洋作戰能力的船隻與船員，1126年的比薩條約與1130至1131年間他派往熱那亞、比薩的使團，都是這種結合的產物。從西方文獻看，阿方索的使團甚至同時接觸了拜占庭與法蒂瑪的使者，兩個基督教世界要在穆斯林的地中海航線上合作，這在敘利亞與巴勒斯坦戰線吃緊的年份裡並非不可能。阿爾穆拉維德方面的理由同樣清楚：1130年11月埃米爾阿里·本·優素福親率大軍渡海攻入西班牙南部，回程時遇上大風，艦隊盡毀，元氣大傷；德安是重建海軍的支點，一旦聯軍奪去港口與船塢，摩洛維王朝在安達盧斯沿海的整條補給線就會被切斷。因此德安不能失，雙方都知道這一點，交鋒本身只是早晚。
causeEn: The reasons for the fight lay half on land and half at sea. Alfonso I, having taken Valencia in 1102 and Tortosa in 1128, drove his land front westward and squeezed the Almoravid positions on the eastern coast of al-Andalus one by one. The defeat at Almenara in 1126 and the truce of Almenara that followed seemed to halt the war, but the terms of that truce never covered anything at sea: the harbour of Valencia and the lanes off it were left unprotected, and the record of Catalan and Sicilian merchant ships being stopped and robbed off Denia runs on and on. The stalemate on land therefore needed a solution at sea; once the water between Valencia and Denia was controlled, the supply line of the crusade, the drive on Toledo and the southern economy of the realm would all profit at once. The push from the cities was a second motive. Pisa and Genoa wanted guaranteed markets and harbour rights on the Christian lanes, and Alfonso needed hulls and crews capable of ocean voyaging; the treaty with Pisa of 1126 and the embassies he sent to Genoa and Pisa in 1130 and 1131 were the product of that combination. From the western documents it also appears that the envoys of Alfonso spoke with the envoys of Byzantium and of the Fatimids in the same years, and that two Christian worlds might work together against the Muslim Mediterranean lane was not impossible in a year when Syria and Palestine were consuming the attention of the crusade. The reasons on the Almoravid side were just as plain. In November 1130 the emir Ali ibn Yusuf personally led a great army across the sea into southern Spain, and on the return passage his fleet was destroyed by a storm, leaving him badly shaken; Denia was the hinge on which a fleet had to be rebuilt, and if the coalition took the port and the shipyards the whole supply line of the Almoravids in coastal al-Andalus would be cut. Denia could not be lost, both sides knew it, and the clash itself was only a matter of time.
impact: 德安之戰沒有改變伊比利亞的版圖，卻改變了誰能在地中海西端開船。對阿拉貢王國而言，這是一個戰略轉折點。阿方索一世經營了十幾年的海上力量在一天之內化為烏有，瓦倫西亞的商人抱怨不斷，比薩與熱那亞的船東把損失記入王室帳上，聯盟的熱情隨之冷卻；王國此後近一個世紀在海上只保留巡哨用的輕舟，直到十三世紀詹姆斯一世才重新組建能遠征的艦隊，重新奪回巴利阿里群島。海上擴張的資源被抽回陸上，用在攻取托列多、鞏固貝達與哈恩的城堡上。對摩洛維王朝而言，這場勝利把瓦倫西亞的海岸線牢牢釘在阿爾穆拉維德一方的手中，德安從此成為他們巡邏巴利阿里海峽、襲擾加泰隆尼亞與塔爾戈沿岸的基地，也讓摩洛維得以把北非的糧食、馬匹與工匠源源運過海來，供應阿爾梅里亞與穆爾西亞的軍隊。第二次十字軍在聖地吃緊的年份，需要用兵於敘利亞，正是這個安全窗口讓安達盧斯海岸得以喘息。技術層面的後果更耐人尋味。希臘火及其同族的含油燃燒物，第一次在西地中海的編年史裡留下大規模使用的記載；配方的核心仍鎖在君士坦丁堡，但「以火船對付密集泊陣的敵艦」的做法從此成為西方地中海海戰的標準選項之一，在十三世紀阿拉貢與熱那亞、威尼斯的衝突裡一再出現。德安也從此在西方地圖上成為「可燒之城」的代名詞，直到十三世紀末瓦倫西亞王國攻取此地，這個名字才從地圖上的敵方基地變成己方港口。
impactEn: The battle of Denia changed no map of Iberia, but it decided who could sail in the western Mediterranean. For the Crown of Aragon it was a strategic turning point. The naval force Alfonso I had been building for more than a decade was destroyed in a single day; the merchants of Valencia complained without end, the Pisan and Genoese shipowners entered their losses in the royal accounts, and the warmth of the alliance cooled. The kingdom kept nothing at sea but a few patrol boats for the next century, and it was not until the thirteenth century and James I that a fleet fit for distant service was rebuilt and the Balearics retaken. The resources meant for maritime expansion were pulled back onto the land, into the taking of Toledo and the fortifying of the castles of Bida and Jaén. For the Almoravid dynasty this victory nailed the Valencian coast to their side. Denia became the base from which they patrolled the Balearic channel and raided the Catalan and Tortosa shore, and it allowed the Almoravids to carry grain, horses and craftsmen out of North Africa without let or hindrance to feed the garrisons of Almeria and Murcia. The Second Crusade was drawing men towards Syria in the very years when the coast of al-Andalus could afford to breathe. The consequences for technique are the most suggestive. Greek fire and its oil-based relatives left their first large-scale record in the chronicles of the western Mediterranean; the core of the formula remained locked in Constantinople, but the practice of sending fire ships against an enemy squadron lying crowded at anchor became a standard option in western Mediterranean sea fighting, and it reappeared in the thirteenth century in the wars of Aragon against Genoa and Venice. Denia also entered western cartography as a name synonymous with a city that could be burned, and only when the Kingdom of Valencia took the place at the end of the thirteenth century did the name change from an enemy base into a harbour of its own.
result: 勝負很清楚：阿爾穆拉維德大勝，基督教聯軍大敗。聯軍攻入德安灣之後損失慘重，艦隊的大半在火船與隨後的登船戰中被焚、被奪，剩餘的船隻在灣內失去編制，各自逃散或被拖走；被俘者以千計。這是十二世紀基督教西班牙一次罕見的、海上規模的大敗，編年史因此把1132年視為摩洛維王朝在安達盧斯海防上的頂點年份之一。但對阿爾穆拉維德而言，勝利是防守性的成功，不是戰略的擴張。德安港完好，碼頭與船塢未毀，聯軍並沒有真正登陸作戰；阿方索的目標是燒掉船塢、奪取港口，這個目標完全沒有達成。摩洛維王朝從北非運來的海上補給線照常運作，瓦倫西亞與巴利阿里海峽的航運安全，瓦倫西亞的穆斯林當局得以把注意力放回西線，去應付1136年瓦倫西亞地區的叛亂以及1147年之後的十字軍攻勢。對阿拉貢王國而言，結果是一個退路：海上的門關上了，於是阿方索把國策收回陸上，城堡、邊境與托列多的遠征取代了艦隊。真正的清算要等到後來——德安最終在十三世紀末落入瓦倫西亞王國手中，聯軍在德安留下的敗績，幾乎直接指出了下一代西班牙海軍從哪裡重新起步：不是從零開始，而是從一座仍然燃著回憶的港口。
resultEn: The outcome was plain: a great Almoravid victory and a great defeat for the Christian coalition. The coalition had entered the bay of Denia and paid dearly for it; the greater part of the fleet was burned or taken in the fire ships and the boarding that followed, the surviving ships lost their order inside the bay and scattered or were dragged off, and the prisoners were counted by the thousand. It was a rare large-scale maritime defeat for Christian Spain in the twelfth century, and the chronicles accordingly treat 1132 as one of the high-water years of Almoravid sea power in al-Andalus. For the Almoravids, however, the victory was a defensive success rather than a strategic expansion. The port of Denia was intact, the quays and shipyards undamaged, and the coalition never really got ashore; Alfonso's aim of burning the shipyards and seizing the harbour was achieved in no part at all. The maritime supply line the Almoravids drew from North Africa ran on unchanged, the lanes between Valencia and the Balearic channel stayed secure, and the Muslim authorities of Valencia could turn their attention back to the western front, to the revolt in the Valencian hinterland in 1136 and to the crusading pressure that came with 1147. For the Crown of Aragon the result was a retreat: the sea door was shut, so Alfonso pulled the policy of the realm back onto the land, and castles, frontiers and the march on Toledo took the place of the fleet. The real reckoning came later, when Denia finally passed to the Kingdom of Valencia at the end of the thirteenth century; the defeat the coalition left at Denia pointed almost directly to where the next Spanish navy would begin: not from nothing, but from a harbour that was still burning with the memory of it.
